newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Industrial action looms in Cyprus shipping dept.
newsitem.headline: Industrial action looms in Cyprus shipping dept.

text.p: Employees in Cyprus's department of merchant shipping will enforce an overtime ban in early October if pay disputes are not resolved and demands for more staff not met, its union said on Thursday.
"We are hoping it won't get to that, but if it does the only party that will be to blame is the Ministry of Finance," union representative Demos Petropoulos told Reuters.

"The authorities can tell an inspector to go to Argentina to work at the weekend but he won't get paid a penny in overtime. The government gets paid by the shipowner though...this is the only government department where overtime pay doesn't exist," he added.

Employees are also seeking the recruitment of merchant shipping officers and better organisation within the department, which comes under the responsibility of the Ministry of Communications and Works.

Merchant shipping employees say that if their demands are not met they will enforce work to rule measures from October 1, just one week before a widely publicised international conference on shipping scheduled to take place on the island.
Maritime Cyprus, a biennial conference, is being organised by the department with the Ministry of Finance, the Central Bank of Cyprus and the Cyprus Shipping Council.
Cyprus's shipping registry is the fifth largest worldwide, consisting of more than 2,600 vessels in excess of 24 million gross tonnes.
